description: Golden reference for calc_accel_magnet.py on the C-type dipole em_1-8_eighth.jou (1/8 model, linear mu_r=1000).
rationale: Regression guard for the 1/8-reduction pipeline (single-axis Kelvin offset + 3-plane webcut + kelvin_far infinity-plane Dirichlet, 2026-04-25).  Verifies: 1/8 is no longer rejected as NotImplementedError, sym_<bc>_<axis> sidesets propagate for all 3 axes, kelvin_far is recognised as Dirichlet by calc_accel_magnet, and (after 2026-04-26 deterministic-anchor fix) NGSolve loads the .vol with all 774/774 Kelvin pairs identified at machine precision.  NOT a physics-accuracy comparison.

sample.generator_cmd_note: Regenerate via Cubit batch: play em_1-8_eighth.jou + play auto_kelvin_entry.py (with RADIA_LAUNCHER_CONFIG containing kelvin_reduction with x=ht=0, y=ht=0, z=bn=0) + export netgen order=2 overwrite.

geometry_note: 1/8 octant: yoke at x>=0, y>=0, z>=0 (no yoke change vs 1/4 since the C-shape is already in y>=0); air 1/8 sphere via intersect with octant brick.  Kelvin offset along x (default = first reduction axis), webcut at x=offset_dist (kelvin_far), y=0 (sym), z=0 (sym).  GND nodeset at Kelvin centre (offset_dist, 0, 0).

observations.note: Absolute-value snapshot for regression guard.  Different sym BCs than em_1-4_quarter_xz (added sym_ht=0_y + kelvin_far Dirichlet), so numbers differ (~3x larger B_origin_mag because the additional Dirichlet planes restrict the field more aggressively).  Coil is full racetrack -- BCs do not match its actual symmetry.  Mesh topology lock refreshed 2026-04-26 after `_add_kelvin_cubit_reduction` deterministic-anchor fix landed: previous numbers (ne=56289, ndof=11695) were from the old `max(curves, key=length)` rule with C++ identification fallback; the deterministic `min(curves, key=(z,y,x))` rule produces a slightly different mesh (ne=56369, ndof=11708) with all 774/774 Kelvin pairs at machine precision (no fallback).  Physics (B_origin_mag, W_mag, L) unchanged within tolerance.
